MEMORANDUM
  Agenda Item #:  6
  Meeting Date: 6-8-2021

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS

THRU:  LAURA GUGLIELMO, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  CAROLYNN PETRU, INTERIM PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE PARKLANDS COMMITTEE
  FOR MAY 13, 2021

DATE:  JUNE 8, 2021

ACTION REQUIRED  CONSENT  X  RECEIVE & FILE

Recommendation

Staff recommends that the City Council approve the actions of the Parklands Committee
for the meeting of May 13, 2021.

Summary

In the Parklands Committee meeting of May 13, 2021, all Committee Members were
present. Six applications were discussed and one application was continued. There were
no public speakers on non-agenda items.

Analysis and Findings

The City held a Parklands Committee meeting on May 13, 2021 and the Committee
recommended the following actions be approved by the City Council.

The Parklands Committee Chair Richie-Bray introduced a request from staff to continue
Item No. 5 (PC-554-21). This application was noticed with inaccurate address; therefore
staff requested continuance of the item to the next meeting in order to allow the
application to be re-noticed to provide a fair review for all residences affected.

  1
 All five Members voted to continue Item No. 5 to the next Parklands Committee meeting
on July 8, 2021.

1. PC-550-21; Application to remove one Canary Island pine located in the parkway
  adjacent to 305 Via Adarme

  Applicant: Lauren Kerns, 305 Via Adarme, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this non-view application as a request to remove one Canary Island pine
for safety. Two large Canary Island pines are planted close to the property line and very
close to each other. The home’s electric service requires sufficient space for the wires not
to be in the branches of the tree and the branches bearing pine cones not to be located
over the roof of the proposed addition or the driveway. The removal of the tree would
reduce dropping pine cones and be a benefit to public safety. Staff indicated the
remaining tree will provide privacy and screening and not affect the neighborhood
character of Coast Live Oak.

The applicant indicated the dropping pine cones were a safety issue for her home and the
driveway, as well as the children that walked this route to Valmonte School.

The Committee Members all agreed and supported removal of the one Canary Island
pine.

Committee Member Groves motioned, second by Committee Member Cooper, to
recommend approval to the City Council. The vote was in favor (5-0). Recommendations
for conditions were not included in the motion and the Urban Forester asked for
clarification. The motion was modified to include the conditions as recommended by
staff.

Committee Member Groves motioned, second by Committee Member Cooper, to
recommend approval to the City Council to remove one Canary Island pine located
adjacent to 305 Via Adarme according to the ‘Standard Conditions For Tree Removal
Approvals,’ including stump grinding, payment of $500 to the ‘Tree Bank’ and a ‘Tree
Removal’ permit issued by the City. The vote was in favor (5-0).

2. PC-551-21; Application to remove one Italian Stone pine located in the parkway
  adjacent to 36 Coronel Plaza

  Applicant: Frank Clark, 36 Coronel Plaza, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this request to remove one Italian stone pine adjacent to the driveway at
36 Coronel Plaza as both a view and safety application. The tree is obscuring the view
from the home and lifting the driveway and curb approximately 2-inches. Trimming is an
option that will increase the view, but will reduce the beauty of the tree. In addition, this
option will not reduce damage to the driveway or the walkway of the property next door.

  2
 The tree is not the neighborhood character, doesn’t provide privacy or screening and has
never been the designated street tree for this location.

The applicant indicated three reasons for the request. Safety for the utilities present,
damage to the driveway/walkway and view obstruction. The tree is not fully grown and
will continue to grow larger. Even with annual trimming, the tree already extends over
the driveway and is at the roof line. Small branches and twigs hit the windows during
wind events and the driveway requires repair.

Two Committee Members indicated the application was a difficult one; stating the tree is
beautiful but has grown out of its space, is not the neighborhood character, is damaging
the driveway and is blocking the view. Discussion ensued concerning possibility of
planting a new street tree in the pine’s place, elsewhere in the yard or in Cornel Plaza.

Committee Member Rhodes motioned, second by Committee Member Cooper to
recommend approval to the City Council to remove one Italian stone pine adjacent to 36
Coronel Plaza according to the ‘Standard Conditions For Tree Removal Approvals,’
including stump grinding, payment of $500 to the ‘Tree Bank’ and a ‘Tree Removal’
permit issued by the City. The vote was in favor (5-0).

3. PC-552-21; Application to remove four Canary Island pines located in the Apsley
  Vista Path adjacent to 1500 Paseo Del Mar

  Applicant: Brett Dillenberg, 1405 Chelsea Road, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274
Staff indicated this view enhancement application requests removal of four Canary Island
pines that are located in Apsley Vista Path. The trees obscure blue ocean water, Catalina
Island, sunset views and the coastline lights from most rooms in the home, as well as for
many adjacent and supporting neighbors. The trees were planted 60-70 years ago without
approval to plant in the Parklands. These pines are not the neighborhood character and
are not necessary for screening or privacy. Staff recommended keeping one pine closest
to 1404 Paseo Del Mar to retain part of the forest to balance tree removal and to possibly
provide some screening for 1404 Paseo Del Mar.

The applicant indicated they wanted to restore the majestic views that existed when they
purchased their home in 1999. Additionally, the trees requested for removal are not
native or ever approved to be planted by the City. The adjacent neighbors on Chelsea
Road and Apsely Road support the request and will benefit from the increased views of
the ocean and coastline lights if the tree are removed. Two additional residents from the
neighborhood spoke in support of the application.

Former Parklands Committee Member and principal author of the ‘Tree Management
Policy’, Charles Petersen spoke is support of removal and added the statement that no
unpermitted tree should be protected and that neighborhood character can only be created
by the planting of approved street trees on the street and not in the Parklands.

  3
 The Committee Members agreed the pines were mature and attractive but found it
difficult to approve removal of all four at one time, except for the fact they blocked the
view. The majority of the Committee agreed the pines should never have been planted in
this location and all four should be removed. They all agreed the trees did not provide
screening, privacy or create neighborhood character.

One member commented on the letter that indicated removal will increase abuses from
vehicles driving through the pathway strip. This is considered a separate issue that should
not affect the request in the application, but should be followed up by staff.

Chair Richie-Bray commented on Mr. Peterson’s statement, indicating that the question
of when to protect or remove the right tree in the right location, even if it was planted
without a permit, needs to be considered and balanced, which is why there is a Parklands
Committee.

Committee Member Groves motioned, second by Committee Member Cooper, to
recommend approval to the City Council to remove four Canary Island pines located in
Apsley Vista Path according to the ‘Standard Conditions For Tree Removal Approvals,’
including removal of the stumps, payment of $2,000 to the ‘Tree Bank’ and a ‘Tree
Removal’ permit issued by the City. The vote was in favor (4-1), with Committee
Member McCabe dissenting.

4. PC-553-21; Application to remove one Aleppo pine, one small Canary Island palm
  and all shrubs located in the Apsley Vista Path between 1501 and 1405 Chelsea Road

  Applicant: Paul R. Markley, 2790 Skypark Dr. Ste. 106, Torrance, CA 90505

Staff introduced this application for view enhancement involving tree and shrub removal
on the Apsley Vista Path as similar to the last application but from a different resident
and different location on Addison Road. One Aleppo pine, one small Canary Island palm
and all shrubs adjacent to 1501 Chelsea road are requested for removal.

Staff indicated the trees and shrubs were safe and healthy. None of the trees or shrubs
were permitted to be planted in the Parklands and none of the trees or shrubs are native or
permitted to be planted on most Parklands. Some of the plants may have started by seeds.
In addition, some of the shrubs are considered invasive weeds and could be removed
solely for that reason.

The Aleppo pine, small Canary Island palm and the shrubbery encroach into the view of
the ocean and coastline lights. Neighborhood character is not affected and safety will be
improved for the neighborhood with increased visibility of activities within the
Parklands. Privacy for 1501 Chelsea Road will be reduced but this resident supports the
application.

The applicant spoke, agreeing with Mr. Petersen’s comments, and added the area was
overgrown and provide a hidden area for drug deals. As for vehicles on the Parklands, he

  4
 observed that they seem to be restricted to the perpendicular alley the runs between the
homes where utilities and gardeners traverse the alley.

All the Committee Members supported the application as presented. Committee Chair
Richie-Bray suggested approving trimming of the Tall Canary Island palm at the same
time the removals are to be performed.

Committee Member Rhodes motioned, second by Committee Member Cooper, to
recommend approval to the City Council to remove one Aleppo pine, one small Canary
Island palm and all shrubbery located in the Apsley Vista Path adjacent to 1501 Chelsea
Road according to the ‘Standard Conditions For Tree Removal approvals,’ including
stump grinding, a payment of $1,000 to the ‘Tree Bank’ and a ‘Tree Removal’ permit
issued by the City. The vote was in favor (5-0).

5. PC-554-21; Application to remove six Eucalyptus trees located in the Cataluna Strip
  behind 1609 to 1649 Cataluna Place
  Applicant: Sulabha and Anil Dave, 2229 Via Cerritos, Palos Verdes Estates, CA
  90274

This application was continued to the next Parklands Committee meeting of July 8, 2021.

6. PC-555-21; Application to waive planting of three of the 12 Kentia palms adjacent to
  720 Paseo Del Mar

  Applicant; Lu Ana Bercier, 720 Paseo Del Mar, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this request to waive planting three of the 12 designated street trees
adjacent to 720 Paseo Del Mar as a view application to protect the existing view corridor
from this residence. A single Brazilian pepper tree is located in the grass area, with the
area to the right of the tree open to the ocean. The neighborhood character will be
enhanced by the planting of the nine Kentia palms, but Kentia palms provide little
screening or privacy if planted appropriately. This is one reason for their designation as
the street tree for Paseo Del Mar.

The Committee Members supported the application, but agreed only to waive two of the
palms that were located directly in the corridor and require the palm adjacent to the
driveway to be planted.

Committee Member Cooper motioned, second by Committee Member Rhodes to
recommend to City Council approval with modification to waive the planting of two of
the 12 Kentia palms located adjacent to 720 Paseo Del Mar and require a $1,000 payment
to the ‘Tree Bank’. The vote was in favor (5-0).

7. PC-CTP-13-21; Concept Plan to enhance the Parklands surrounding George Allen
  Baseball Field with native plants and walking paths.

  5
   Applicant: George Allen Neighborhood Association - Ghazala Kahn, 1512 Via
  Lopez, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff provided a summary describing the current state of George Allen Field and the
Parklands Use Policy factors that needed to be considered by the Parklands Committee.
The request included native trees, shrubs, seasonal flowers and ground covers. The
purpose is to provide a safe and attractive off-street walking path and improve the visual
appearance of the neighborhood. The installation, management and ongoing monthly
maintenance of the enhancements will be funded by the Association and be performed by
professional contractors.

In kind services from the City are requested that include rock donations and delivery, use
of the existing water meter with the water cost paid by the City, mulch deliveries to
suppress weeds and dust, planting of street trees in the perimeter right-of-ways, and
continued weed abatement of the areas not landscaped. Installation of an asphalt parking
lot for use of the baseball field by the City or Peninsula Junior League Baseball is also
requested. The tentative timeline for improvements are planned to begin in 2022.

The Association representative, Marlene Breene, presented a PowerPoint presentation
showing the conceptual plan and suggested plant palette, and indicated the Association
will fund raise if the conceptual concept plan is approved.

Speakers discussed the plant palette and suggested considering options other than native
plants or a mixture of natives and Mediterranean plants to blend with the existing private
landscapes of the adjacent homes.

The Committee Members all supported the concept and Chair Richie-Bray provided
additional concepts to consider that included more active recreational elements, such as
an additional baseball field or a soccer field.

The Association representative, Marlene Breene indicated the plan follows the Parklands
Use Policy that requires use of native plants. The applicant, Ghazala Kahn indicated the
Association was not interested in another sports facility, but wanted to enhance the
perimeter of the property to beautify and enable passive use of the park.

The Committee Members all agreed the project concept should be developed further and
a final plan submitted for review that is based on the Committee’s discussion.

The meeting was adjourned at 9:30PM to July 8, 2021.

Notification

These matters have been agenized and posted in the routine manner.

Carl Moritz
